questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A place where i could challenge myself and experience different landscapes and nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: An orientation seminar

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was staying at a "Uniflat" arranged by the university.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I am pretty sure all exchange students who applies to Uniflats gets somewhere to stay. I think the monthly pay was about 4500 DKK. All Uniflats has a "Kiwihost", a student from New Zealand living there as well. We were 6 persons in total, 5 international and one kiwi.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We lived in a smal 3 storage house, it was quite cozy, but a little low on light and a bit worn out.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I remember it as straight forward.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Both the academic staff and the Uniflats staff were easy to get hold of.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull, i had to get special permissions for two courses, which i got. One of them at pretty late notice, though.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You don't have to stress about the courses, when you've gotten in. You are able to change them the first couple weeks of the semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was on my third year of my bachelor-program, and i took a 400-level paper which were completely fine difficulty-wise.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Pretty similar except for two big differences. 1 All lectures was recorded (powerpoint with the lecturer talking over), which made it a little too easy to skip class. 2 They had far more hand-ins during the course, than i'm used to at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
POLS324 Current Issues in Environmental Politics
GEOG460 Climatology
MAOR102 Māori Society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I'd really recommend: "Current Issues in Environmental Politics". It was a very interesting course, i learned a lot about justice and decolonial theory and how to apply it to environmental problematics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I spent a lot of money at cafes, on fast food and on booze.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee and fast food was less expensive than Denmark, cigarettes and alcohol cost more than DK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I only participated in a salsa course, and they have a free of charge fitness-center on campus, which i used a lot.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost everything, i know that the outdoor-tour (tramping) club was popular and planned some nice trips, there was a lot of political and specific subject / education related clubs as well.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Be aware: Dunedin is a party-town. I didn't know beforehand, but ended up enjoying it (and i would describe myself as a regular 25 year old dane).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go see as much of the natural surroundings as possible -it's impossible to experience it all. I really enjoyed the Catleins and Queenstown myself. If you have time for it, the north island is beautiful as well -especially Tongariro and the thermic area around Rotaroa is worth a visit.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it easy, it's not too different from Europe but more than i expected. The kiwi's are generally very easy-going.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The international environment is very big and easy to connect with. Not a lot of kiwis shows up to class, but those who does are usually talkative in my experience. To be honest, i primarily hung out with my flatmates friend group of locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: In NZ it's common to start uni around 18 years old, so there was a lot of very young, very drunk people especially at semester-start. They were harmless of course, but it surprised me a little in the beginning.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the effort of the university to include and respect Māori worldviews. In general get to talk to as many Māori students and learn as much as possible about their culture. It opened up for a lot of perspectives for me and i got very inspired by it.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be openminded, enjoy your freetime, spend your energy where you are physically -instead of your head being back home in DK.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really, no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The hikes in the mountains, the friends i made and the way i developed myself during my stay.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Honestly, homesickness. It's difficult not being home for special occasions and tough times for your dear ones.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
